name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +15 point partisan lean
Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with a large financial advantage
Republican Robert Burke has raised no money and is in debt
Prediction markets price Lynch at about 97% to win
model.rationale: Lynch is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 15 points, while Burke has raised nothing and carries negative cash on hand. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Lynch win, so the forecast stays near the baseline margin of roughly 22 points.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against Lynch or an unexpected polling shift would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Stephen Lynch, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Boston-area district that leans Democratic by 15 points. He has raised over $900,000 and holds more than $640,000 on hand, though outside groups have spent modestly against him.

Republican Robert Burke has raised no money and reports negative cash on hand, leaving him with little visible campaign infrastructure. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks resources. With no public polls and no expert ratings, the race rests on fundamentals, which overwhelmingly favor Lynch. Prediction markets price his chances at roughly 97 percent, consistent with a comfortable double-digit win.
